input.subject: Build a defensive local-security lab: a consent-based home lab for isolating owned devices, inventorying listening services, observing network metadata, and running a contained decoy.
input.entryReader: Has used a terminal and owns their home router. Has never watched their own network traffic.
input.notGiven: No page count, no outline, and no existing page content are inputs to this run.

perspectives.view: Know what you own and what it exposes before adding tools. Inventory comes first.
Isolation is a routing and firewall property you verify, not a feature name on a router box.
Sensors produce either connection records or rule alerts. Both need a copy of the traffic and both need tuning.
A decoy is only useful if touching it is always suspicious, and only safe if it can't become a launch point.
Owning a network does not give unlimited authority to capture what crosses it. Consent defines the lab.

concepts.name: Consent and scope
concepts.summary: Which devices and traffic you may observe. Other people's traffic on your network is not automatically yours to capture.

concepts.name: Threat model
concepts.summary: What you are protecting, from whom, and which failure you care about most. Decides what the lab watches.

concepts.name: IP addresses and subnets
concepts.summary: Private address ranges, subnet boundaries, and how a device knows what is local.

concepts.name: What a home router does
concepts.summary: Routes between the home network and the internet, hands out addresses, and translates addresses (NAT).

concepts.name: NAT is not a firewall
concepts.summary: NAT blocks unsolicited inbound traffic as a side effect of mapping state, not as a policy. IPv6 often has no NAT at all.

concepts.name: Ports, sockets, and listening
concepts.summary: A process listens on an address and port. The bind address decides who can reach it.

concepts.name: Admin commands
concepts.summary: Running inspection commands with elevated rights on Linux, macOS, and Windows, and reading their output.

concepts.name: Packets versus connection metadata
concepts.summary: Full packets carry content. Connection records carry who, when, how much, and which protocol. Metadata is smaller and less invasive.

concepts.name: Device inventory
concepts.summary: A list of every device you own on the network, with owner and purpose. You cannot defend what you haven't listed.

concepts.name: Why small devices matter
concepts.summary: Cameras and routers with default credentials were enlisted by the Mirai botnet at massive scale.

concepts.name: Listener inventory
concepts.summary: Listing listening services per host, with process, bind address, port, and reason it exists.

concepts.name: Baseline and diff
concepts.summary: A dated record of normal, re-taken after intentional changes, so unknown changes stand out.

concepts.name: Firewall rules
concepts.summary: Allow and deny policy, stateful tracking, default-deny inbound.

concepts.name: Testing a firewall from both sides
concepts.summary: A rule is only proven when you try the blocked path from each side and see it fail.

concepts.name: UPnP and silent port forwards
concepts.summary: Devices can ask the router to open inbound ports automatically. Guidance is to disable UPnP on the router.

concepts.name: Segmentation
concepts.summary: Zones, VLANs, and guest networks. A Wi-Fi repeater extends a network; it does not isolate one.

concepts.name: Lab boundary
concepts.summary: Putting the lab behind a router you control, downstream of the household network.

concepts.name: Verifying isolation
concepts.summary: Proving the lab cannot reach trusted devices, and recording the proof.

concepts.name: Getting a copy of traffic
concepts.summary: Mirror (SPAN) ports on a managed switch, or taps. A sensor sees nothing it isn't given.

concepts.name: Zeek
concepts.summary: Turns traffic into connection and protocol logs for understanding normal behavior.

concepts.name: Suricata
concepts.summary: Rule-based alerts plus EVE JSON records. HOME_NET must be set correctly or alerts flood.

concepts.name: Choosing a sensor
concepts.summary: Metadata-first versus alert-first, matched to the threat model and hardware.

concepts.name: Alert triage and tuning
concepts.summary: Most first alerts are noise. Installation is the start; tuning is the work.

concepts.name: What the lab records, and for how long
concepts.summary: Logs contain other people's metadata. Decide retention and review before collecting.

concepts.name: What a decoy is
concepts.summary: A service nobody should touch, so any touch is a signal. Low-interaction versus high-interaction.

concepts.name: Decoy containment
concepts.summary: Isolated zone, outbound denied, no real secrets. A compromised decoy must not become a launch point.

concepts.name: Running a decoy
concepts.summary: Deploying OpenCanary (lightweight, alert-only) or Cowrie (SSH/Telnet emulation) inside the contained zone.

concepts.name: Reviewing decoy activity
concepts.summary: Reading decoy alerts against the baseline and deciding what a touch means.

misconceptions.claim: My router's NAT is a firewall.
misconceptions.correction: NAT's inbound blocking is a side effect of mapping state, not a policy, and IPv6 frequently skips NAT entirely.

misconceptions.claim: A guest network isolates my devices.
misconceptions.correction: Isolation depends on the router's actual rules; guest networks vary and some share more than expected. Verify it.

misconceptions.claim: A Wi-Fi extender makes a separate network.
misconceptions.correction: A repeater extends the same network. Isolation needs routing and firewall rules.

misconceptions.claim: If I didn't open a port, none is open.
misconceptions.correction: UPnP lets devices open inbound ports on their own.

misconceptions.claim: A sensor anywhere on the network sees everything.
misconceptions.correction: A sensor sees only traffic it is given; it needs a mirror port or tap on the right segment.

misconceptions.claim: It's my network, so I can capture anything on it.
misconceptions.correction: Ownership does not grant unlimited legal authority to intercept other people's communications.

misconceptions.claim: A listening service is only a problem if it's on the internet.
misconceptions.correction: A service bound to all interfaces is reachable by every device on the local network, including compromised ones.

edgeCases.case: Double NAT when the lab router sits behind the household router.
IPv6 on by default gives devices globally routable addresses.
Shared housing: other people's devices on the same network are out of scope.
Encrypted traffic limits what a sensor can read, which pushes toward metadata.
Small hardware (a Raspberry Pi) may drop packets under full capture.

realWorldFailures.failure: Mirai botnet: IoT devices with factory default credentials enlisted for record-scale DDoS attacks in 2016.
UPnProxy: attackers injected NAT rules through exposed UPnP on consumer routers to turn them into proxies.
realWorldFailures.lesson: Know and control what can open ports.

realWorldFailures.failure: Compromised honeypots used to attack systems outside the honeynet, the reason honeynets require data control.
Home Suricata installs flooding with false positives when HOME_NET is misconfigured.
